newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta spot natural gas prices hold, B.C. drops.
newsitem.headline: Alberta spot natural gas prices hold, B.C. drops.

text.p: Most Canadian spot natural gas prices were little changed on Wednesday as Alberta players continued to live with less-than-expected supply.
But in British Columbia, prices fell amid too much gas.
Spot gas at the AECO storage up in Alberta was quated at about C$1.49 per gigajoule, up one or two cents from Tuesday and three cents from a week ago.
August AECO was talked at C$1.47/1.48 per GJ, up from C$1.46/1.465 yesterday, traders said.

A Calgary-based marketer said the market was bracing for the effects of work on NOVA's Princess A compressor in Alberta, which was expected to result in cutbacks in interruptible volumes at Empress and reduced injections at AECO.

But, other than a 120 million cubic foot per day drop in injections between Monday and Tuesday, from 1.1 billion cubic feet to 990 million cubic feet a day, the market had yet to experience any impact, the trader said.
Meanwhile, field receipts continued to lag NOVA's target average of 12.5 billion cubic feet per day by about 600 millin cubic feet a day, he said.

In the British Columbia market, Sumas spot prices fell into the low to mid-US$0.90s per million British thermal unit range, as storage injections were restricted, market sources said. That was down from US$0.98/1.00 on Tuesday and US$1.04/1.09 last week. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
